added_lemmas.statement: In the canonical lvLiNGAM model of Tramontano, Kivva, Salehkaleybar, Kiyavash, and Drton, the observed coordinates are linear mixtures of mutually independent, nondegenerate, non-Gaussian exogenous coordinates.  Their order-\(r\) cumulant parameterization allows an unrestricted diagonal source-cumulant tensor at each retained order.  Their Figure~3 is the single-proxy graph on \(Z,T,Y\) with \(\ell\) latent common causes and the directed edges \(Z\to T\to Y\).  Theorems~3.1 and 3.4--3.5 give, respectively, the bivariate root construction and proxy-effect sufficiency through order \(k(\ell)\), while Theorem~3.6 claims failure of order-three identification when \(\ell=1\).

attestation.note: Checked against the PMLR 267 published PDF, Section 2.2, Figure 3, and the displayed statements of Theorems 3.1 and 3.4--3.6. A stable source handle is supplied because the node paraphrases several separately located statements.

added_lemmas.statement: The normalized graph chart in \(\Theta_{\ell,R}\) is the centered, generic-nonzero, realizable finite-atomic truncation of the same canonical single-proxy lvLiNGAM graph used by Tramontano, Kivva, Salehkaleybar, Kiyavash, and Drton.  It is a subclass of their actual-law class through order \(R\), whereas their unrestricted diagonal-cumulant parameter space is algebraically larger because it does not impose positive second cumulants or simultaneous cross-order moment realizability.  Centering changes neither \(C_r\) for \(r\ge2\) nor \(\beta\).  Consequently every independent finite-support converse twin constructed in \(\Theta_{\ell,R}\) is also an actual-law twin in their class, and the proxy-anchored upper-contraction algebra remains valid on their unrestricted diagonal-cumulant chart wherever its displayed rank and denominator factors are nonzero.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The cited canonical parameterization identifies the published graph and its diagonal source-cumulant coordinates.  Under \texttt{ass:graph}, absorb each nonzero \(a_i\) into \(L_i\), as permitted by \texttt{ass:nonzero-graph}.  The five types of normalized mixing columns are then
\[
 (1,\gamma,\beta\gamma)^{\mathsf T},\qquad
 (1,u_i,v_i)^{\mathsf T}\ (i\in I_\ell),\qquad
 (0,1,\beta)^{\mathsf T},\qquad (0,0,1)^{\mathsf T}.
\]
These are exactly the columns obtained from the cited canonical graph: proxy disturbance, latent common causes, treatment disturbance, and outcome disturbance.  Conversely, the final clause of \texttt{def:legal-parameter-domain} gives \(a_i=1\), \(b_i=u_i-\gamma\), and \(c_i=v_i-\beta u_i\); its nonvanishing condition is precisely the generic nonzero-edge restriction.  Thus the graph charts agree after the published scaling normalization.

By \texttt{ass:independence}, multilinearity of cumulants and vanishing of mixed cumulants of independent families give the diagonal sum in \texttt{def:cumulant-map}.  The published algebraic chart permits the diagonal entry at each order to range independently over the ground field.  In contrast, \texttt{def:legal-parameter-domain} requires \(m^S_{j,2}>0\) and one nonnegative atomic probability measure whose moments simultaneously generate all \(\kappa^S_{j,r}\), \(2\le r\le R\).  Hence the latter is contained in the published actual-law truncation and is generally a proper semialgebraic subset of the unrestricted diagonal algebraic chart.

For any scalar random variable \(S\), any constant \(a\), and every \(r\ge2\), translation invariance of cumulants gives \(\operatorname{Cum}_r(S-a)=\operatorname{Cum}_r(S)\).  Replacing every exogenous coordinate by its centered version therefore only translates the observed variables; it preserves all retained cumulants, every structural slope, and in particular \(\beta\).  A nondegenerate finitely supported scalar law is non-Gaussian, and products of the independently chosen source laws preserve mutual independence.  Thus every finite-support twin in the legal domain belongs to the cited actual-law class.  Finally, the factorization and contraction arguments use only the displayed mixing columns, diagonal cumulant additivity, rank, and a nonzero denominator.  They impose no cross-order moment relation.  The same polynomial algebra therefore holds on the cited unrestricted diagonal chart on the stated nonvanishing locus.  This proves every assertion.

added_lemmas.statement:
For \(\ell=2\), one has \(r_\beta(2)=3\).  More explicitly, for a legal order-three observable tuple \(\zeta\), let \(M_3=(\operatorname{Cum}(Z,X_a,X_b))_{a,b=1}^3\).  For a candidate \(q\in\mathbb R\), put
\[
 H(q)=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&1&0\\0&-q&1\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad M(q)=H(q)M_3H(q)^{\mathsf T},
\]
\[
 \nu(q)=\begin{pmatrix}
 \operatorname{Cum}(Z,Z)\\
 \operatorname{Cum}(Z,T)\\
 \operatorname{Cum}(Z,Y-qT)
 \end{pmatrix},\qquad
 h(q)=\begin{pmatrix}
 \operatorname{Cum}(Z,T,Y-qT)\\
 \operatorname{Cum}(T,T,Y-qT)\\
 \operatorname{Cum}(T,Y-qT,Y-qT)
 \end{pmatrix},
\]
and \(s(q)=\operatorname{Cum}(T,Y-qT)\).  Define the observable polynomial
\[
 \mathcal P_\zeta(q)=\det M(q)\,s(q)-\nu(q)^{\mathsf T}\operatorname{adj}(M(q))h(q),
 \qquad a_0(\zeta)=\mathcal P_\zeta(0),\quad
 a_1(\zeta)=\mathcal P_\zeta(1)-\mathcal P_\zeta(0).
\]
On \(\mathcal O_{2,3}\), \(\mathcal P_\zeta(q)=a_0(\zeta)+a_1(\zeta)q\).  The polynomial
\[
 \Delta_{2,3}(\zeta)=\det(M_3)\,a_1(\zeta)
\]
is not identically zero on the legal image.  On the nonempty relatively Zariski-open chart \(\mathcal O_{2,3}\cap\{\Delta_{2,3}\ne0\}\), the terminating totalized recovery rule is
\[
 \zeta\longmapsto -\frac{a_0(\zeta)}{a_1(\zeta)},
\]
and it equals \(\beta(\theta)\) for every \(\theta\in F_{2,3}(\zeta)\); off this chart the rule returns \(\bot\).  The same rule applied to the order-three marginal of \(C_{\le R}\) identifies \(\beta\) for every \(R\ge3\) on the inverse image of this chart.  After localizing the complete two-representation incidence ideal by \(\Delta_{2,3}\), its \(\beta\)-projection has the linear rational-univariate representation \(a_1q+a_0=0\), with the single real root \(-a_0/a_1\); saturation by \(\beta-\beta'\) gives the unit ideal.  Thus the mandatory \((\ell,R)=(2,3)\) test has no nonsingular positive-variance unequal-effect branch.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(\theta\in\Theta_{2,3}\) and write its effect as \(\beta\).  Set
\[
 W=Y-\beta T,qquad
 r_0=(1,\gamma,0)^{\mathsf T},\quad
 r_i=(1,u_i,v_i-\beta u_i)^{\mathsf T}\ (i=1,2),quad
 V=(r_0\ r_1\ r_2).
\]
Let \(\lambda_r=(\kappa^S_{0,r},\kappa^S_{1,r},\kappa^S_{2,r})^{\mathsf T}\), let \(\Lambda_3=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_3)\), and write \(\kappa^S_{t,r}\) for the treatment-disturbance cumulant.  These objects are defined by \texttt{def:cumulant-map}, which follows from \texttt{ass:graph} and \texttt{ass:independence}.

For a candidate \(q\), put \(\delta=\beta-q\) and
\[
 H_\delta=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&1&0\\0&\delta&1\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad V_q=H_\delta V,qquad e_q=H_\delta(0,1,0)^{\mathsf T}=(0,1,\delta)^{\mathsf T}.
\]
The coordinates \((Z,T,Y-qT)\) equal \((Z,T,W+\delta T)\).  Because both disturbance columns \((0,1,\beta)^{\mathsf T}\) and \((0,0,1)^{\mathsf T}\) have zero \(Z\)-coordinate, the proxy-anchored third-cumulant matrix is
\[
 M(q)=V_q\Lambda_3V_q^{\mathsf T}. \tag{1}
\]
Likewise, only the three sources entering \(Z\) contribute to the proxy-anchored covariance vector, so
\[
 \nu(q)=V_q\lambda_2. \tag{2}
\]

Assume first that \(D:=\det(M_3)\ne0\).  Since \(H(q)\) and \(H_\delta\) have determinant one, \(\det M(q)=D\).  Equation~(1) then forces both \(V_q\) and \(\Lambda_3\) to be invertible.  Define
\[
 z_q=\bigl(s_j(t_j+\delta s_j)\bigr)_{j=0}^2,
 \quad (s_0,t_0)=(\gamma,0),quad
 (s_i,t_i)=(u_i,v_i-\beta u_i).
\]
For the three sources entering \(Z\), the three entries of \(h(q)\) are respectively the sums of \(s_j(t_j+\delta s_j)\) times the coordinates \(1,s_j,t_j+\delta s_j\).  The treatment disturbance contributes \(0,\kappa^S_{t,3}\delta,\kappa^S_{t,3}\delta^2\), and the outcome disturbance contributes zero because each entry contains \(T\).  Hence
\[
 h(q)=V_q\Lambda_3z_q+\kappa^S_{t,3}\delta e_q. \tag{3}
\]
The same source-by-source calculation at order two gives
\[
 s(q)=\lambda_2^{\mathsf T}z_q+\kappa^S_{t,2}\delta. \tag{4}
\]
Combining (1)--(4) and using \(\operatorname{adj}(M(q))=D M(q)^{-1}\), one obtains
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \frac{\mathcal P_\zeta(q)}{D}
 &=s(q)-\nu(q)^{\mathsf T}M(q)^{-1}h(q)\\
 &=\delta\left(\kappa^S_{t,2}-\kappa^S_{t,3}
 \lambda_2^{\mathsf T}\Lambda_3^{-1}V_q^{-1}e_q\right).
 \end{aligned} \tag{5}
\]
But \(V_q=H_\delta V\) and \(e_q=H_\delta(0,1,0)^{\mathsf T}\), whence
\[
 V_q^{-1}e_q=V^{-1}(0,1,0)^{\mathsf T}. \tag{6}
\]
The bracket in (5) is therefore independent of \(q\).  With
\[
 K=\kappa^S_{t,2}-\kappa^S_{t,3}\lambda_2^{\mathsf T}
 \Lambda_3^{-1}V^{-1}(0,1,0)^{\mathsf T},
\]
equations (5)--(6) prove the exact factorization
\[
 \mathcal P_\zeta(q)=D(\beta-q)K. \tag{7}
\]
Although \(K\) was expressed using the chosen representation, the left side of (7) is formed from the observed tensors alone.  In particular it is affine in \(q\), \(a_1=-DK\), and, whenever \(Da_1\ne0\), its unique real or complex root is
\[
 \beta=-\frac{a_0}{a_1}. \tag{8}
\]
More explicitly, after substituting the polynomial cumulant map, every coefficient of \(q^m\) with \(m\ge2\) in \(\mathcal P_\zeta(q)\) is a polynomial in the structural coordinates and source cumulants.  Equation~(7) makes each such coefficient vanish on the Zariski-open locus \(\det(V)\prod_{j=0}^2\kappa^S_{j,3}\ne0\), and the explicit specialization below shows that this locus is nonempty.  Polynomial continuation therefore makes all those coefficients vanish identically on the whole algebraic model image.  This proves the asserted affinity even at image points where \(D=0\); recovery itself remains restricted to \(Da_1\ne0\).

This proves full-fiber rather than representation-specific identification.  Indeed, let \(\theta'\in F_{2,3}(\zeta)\) be arbitrary and write \(\beta'=\beta(\theta')\).  The observed condition \(D\ne0\) also forces the analogue of \(V\) and \(\Lambda_3\) for \(\theta'\) to be invertible.  Repeating (1)--(7) for \(\theta'\) gives \(\mathcal P_\zeta(\beta')=0\).  Since \(a_1\ne0\), (8) yields \(\beta'=\beta\).  In the two-representation incidence ring this argument is the polynomial certificate
\[
 a_0+a_1\beta=0,qquad a_0+a_1\beta'=0,qquad
 a_1(\beta-\beta')=0.
\]
This also certifies the requested label-symmetry quotient.  On \(u_1\ne u_2\), write \(e_1=u_1+u_2\), \(e_2=u_1u_2\), and let \(v_i=h_0+h_1u_i\); the last two coefficients exist uniquely because two distinct affine points determine a line.  The complete order-two and order-three source cumulants enter their tensor equations linearly, and eliminating them gives the usual six invariant equations in \((\beta,\gamma,e_1,e_2,h_0,h_1)\).  The displayed relation \(a_0+a_1\beta=0\) is symmetric in the two latent columns and was derived from all tensor entries needed to reconstruct the mixed quadratic \(s(q)\) through the full proxy-anchored matrix, not from a selected factor of a univariate basis element.  Thus every solution of the six-equation quotient on the loading, graph, \(u_1-u_2\), and \(\Delta_{2,3}\) localization obeys the same linear equation.  Conversely the nonempty original fiber supplies its root.  Hence the complete target projection, rather than merely one necessary polynomial with several roots, is the singleton in (8).

After localization at \(\Delta_{2,3}=Da_1\), adjoining and saturating by \(\beta-\beta'\) therefore yields \(1\).  Equivalently, the target FGLM basis is the single monic equation \(q+a_0/a_1=0\).  At the exact integral specialization below, reduction modulo \(101\) gives \(50(2-q)=0\), whose monic modular basis is \(q-2=0\); rational reconstruction is again \(q-2\).  Equation~(7) supplies the characteristic-zero certificate for the generic linear form, so no probabilistic modular inference is being used.  Since the fiber is nonempty and its effect coordinate is the root in (8), the complete target projection has precisely the stated linear rational-univariate representation.  In particular there is no second real branch to which moment-feasibility constraints could be applied.

It remains to show that the chart is nonempty in the legal real domain.  Take
\[
 \beta=2,quad\gamma=1,quad (u_1,v_1)=(3,7),quad (u_2,v_2)=(4,10),
\]
and assign order-two cumulants \((2,5,7,11,13)\) and order-three cumulants \((1,2,3,4,5)\), in the source order \((0,1,2,t,y)\).  Then \(u_1-\gamma=2\), \(u_2-\gamma=3\), \(v_1-\beta u_1=1\), and \(v_2-\beta u_2=2\), so every graph factor is nonzero.  In the \((Z,T,W)\) coordinates,
\[
 V=\begin{pmatrix}1&1&1\\1&3&4\\0&1&2\end{pmatrix},qquad
 \det V=1,qquad \det M_3=(\det V)^2(1)(2)(3)=6.
\]
Solving \(Vx=(0,1,0)^{\mathsf T}\) gives \(x=(-1,2,-1)^{\mathsf T}\), and hence
\[
 \lambda_2^{\mathsf T}\Lambda_3^{-1}V^{-1}(0,1,0)^{\mathsf T}
 =(2,5,7)\operatorname{diag}(1,1/2,1/3)(-1,2,-1)^{\mathsf T}
 =\frac23.
\]
Thus \(K=11-4(2/3)=25/3\),
\[
 \mathcal P_\zeta(q)=50(2-q),\qquad a_1=-50,qquad
 \Delta_{2,3}=-300\ne0. \tag{9}
\]
Every pair \((\kappa_2,\kappa_3)\) in this example, and indeed every pair with \(\kappa_2>0\), is realized by a centered two-point law.  To verify this without an additional hypothesis, put \(d=\kappa_3/\kappa_2\), choose the positive numbers
\[
 A=\frac{d+\sqrt{d^2+4\kappa_2}}2,qquad
 B=\frac{-d+\sqrt{d^2+4\kappa_2}}2,
\]
and give \(A\) probability \(B/(A+B)\) and \(-B\) probability \(A/(A+B)\).  Direct calculation gives mean zero, variance \(AB=\kappa_2\), and third cumulant \(AB(A-B)=\kappa_3\).  Choosing these five laws independently produces legal, nondegenerate, non-Gaussian, finite-support sources.  Zero-weight repetitions embed each two-atom witness into the \(K_3\)-indexed presentation required by \(\Theta_{2,3}\).  Moreover the feasible order-two--three region \(\{(\kappa_2,\kappa_3):\kappa_2>0\}\) is Euclidean open.  Together with the open nonzero graph-coordinate conditions, this makes the legal parameter set Zariski dense in its ambient irreducible affine parameter space.  Its polynomial image therefore has irreducible Zariski closure.  Since (9) shows that \(\Delta_{2,3}\) is not identically zero on that image, its zero locus has empty relative Zariski interior.  Hence the nonvanishing locus in (9) is a nonempty relatively Zariski-open dense part of the legal image, and no Zariski-dense relatively open legal unequal-effect chamber can avoid it.

The displayed determinant, adjugate, and two evaluations at \(q=0,1\) require finitely many field operations, so the recovery rule terminates.  Projection from \(C_{\le R}\) to \(C_{\le3}\) proves the same upper statement for every \(R\ge3\).  Finally, \texttt{thm:generic-lower-fibers} gives \(L_2\le r_\beta(2)\); from the definition of \(L_\ell\), \(L_2=3\).  Together with the order-three recovery just proved, this yields \(r_\beta(2)=3\).
added_lemmas.justification: The mandatory finite-fiber elbow is settled by an observable linear target eliminant, not by a selected numerical root.
added_lemmas.gap: The published sufficient order is \(k(2)=6\), and generic finite-to-one behavior at order three had left a possible disconnected real unequal-effect branch.
added_lemmas.consumer: For two latent confounders, CEId-from-Moments may stop at third-order cumulants and can report the explicit determinant-slope instability certificate.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Determine the finite value of \(r_\beta(\ell)\) exactly for every \(\ell\ge4\).  Using \(\mathfrak H_{\ell}\), classify each unresolved intermediate order \(L_\ell\le R<U_\ell\).  At every order where \(\beta\) is generically constant on legal fibers, give a terminating algebraic recovery atlas whose domains cover a nonempty relatively Zariski-open subset of \(\mathcal O_{\ell,R}\), whose covering charts return the common effect, and whose uncovered legal inputs return \(\bot\).  At every smaller unresolved order, construct a Zariski-dense relatively Euclidean-open subset of the legal image whose fibers contain independent finite-support unequal-\(\beta\) twins.  The first remaining elbow is \((\ell,R)=(4,3)\): decide its complete saturated target projection and certify every surviving real branch against the finite-atomic moment constraints.  The established exact values are \(r_\beta(1)=r_\beta(2)=3\) and \(r_\beta(3)=4\), so none of these cases remains part of the question.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The mandatory \((\ell,R)=(2,3)\) saturation now has an exact linear target projection and proves \(r_\beta(2)=3\). Keeping that case open would be false; the honest residual begins with the unresolved \((4,3)\) elbow and the remaining \(\ell\ge4\) frontier.

proposed.statement: For every \(\ell\ge1\), \(\mathcal O_{\ell,U_{\ell}}\ne\varnothing\), the terminating construction returns a nonempty finite atlas \(\mathfrak A^{\mathrm{id}}_{\ell,U_{\ell}}\), and \(\bigcup_{\chi\in\mathfrak A^{\mathrm{id}}_{\ell,U_{\ell}}}(\mathcal U_{\chi}\cap\mathcal O_{\ell,U_{\ell}})\) contains a nonempty relatively Zariski-open subset of the legal image. For every \(\zeta\) in that union and every atlas chart \(\chi\) covering \(\zeta\), \(\operatorname{rank}(A_{U_{\ell},d_{\chi}})=\ell+1\), \(g_{\chi}(\zeta)\in\mathbb R\), and \(g_{\chi}(\zeta)=\beta(\theta)\) for all \(\theta\in F_{\ell,U_{\ell}}(\zeta)\). For every legal \(\zeta\) outside that union all atlas charts return \(\bot\), so the simultaneous vanishing of the listed discriminants is an explicit failure certificate, not a point estimate. Consequently \(r_{\beta}(\ell)\in\mathbb Z_{\ge2}\) and \(r_{\beta}(\ell)\le U_{\ell}<k(\ell)=(\ell+2)+\lceil(-3+\sqrt{8\ell+17})/2\rceil\).
proposed.justification: This is the constructive strict improvement over the published sufficient depth and provides an observable instability certificate.
proposed.gap: Tramontano et al., Theorems 3.4--3.5, guarantee identification only through the larger pairwise-recovery order \(k(\ell)\).
proposed.consumer: CEId-from-Moments can lower its required empirical moment order and return \(\bot\) with the simultaneous-discriminant certificate whenever no recovery chart covers the observed cumulants.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The orchestrator requires the published-class bridge to be explicit in the upper theorem's proof spine; the claim itself is unchanged.

proposed.statement:
For \(\ell=1\), \(r_\beta(1)=3\).  On a nonempty relatively Zariski-open subset of \(\mathcal O_{1,3}\), \(M_3\) has rank two; if \(f\ne0\) spans its kernel and \(\operatorname{Cum}(f(X),T,T)\ne0\), then every nonempty legal fiber satisfies
\[
 \beta=\frac{\operatorname{Cum}(f(X),T,Y)}{\operatorname{Cum}(f(X),T,T)}.
\]
At order two there is a Zariski-dense relatively Euclidean-open subset of \(\mathcal O_{1,2}\) such that every covariance tuple in that subset has a real one-parameter legal fiber on which \(\beta\) varies; the sources along these fibers may be chosen independent, centered, non-Gaussian, and finitely supported.
proposed.justification: The first exact case both validates the annihilator and prevents algebraic polynomial degree from being mistaken for legal statistical multiplicity.
proposed.gap: Tramontano et al., Theorem 3.6, computes an algebraic quadratic effect projection; the new result audits the legal source-moment domain and shows that polynomial degree two does not furnish a second legal preimage.
proposed.consumer: The one-latent branch of CEId-from-Moments can use third rather than fourth cumulants.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The orchestrator requires the class comparison supporting the one-latent correction to be part of the declared proof spine; the claim itself is unchanged.

proposed.statement: If \(\binom{R+2}{2}\le\ell+3\), then there is a Zariski-dense relatively Euclidean-open subset of \(\mathcal O_{\ell,R}\), contained in the image of legal finite-support parameter points, such that every \(\zeta\) in that subset has a curve in the nonempty fiber \(F_{\ell,R}(\zeta)\) along which \(\beta\) varies. Consequently \(L_{\ell}\le r_{\beta}(\ell)\le U_{\ell}\) and \(r_{\beta}(\ell)/\sqrt{2\ell}\to1\).
proposed.justification: The lower bound is robust on a legal moment chart rather than resting on one algebraic or nonreal witness.
proposed.gap: Neither the anchor nor generic dimension counting constructs real independent-source unequal-effect fibers on an open legal region.
proposed.consumer: The asymptotic square-root frontier determines how the minimum data moment order scales with latent complexity.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The finite-support converse must explicitly carry the bridge showing that its legal twins transfer to the published actual-law class; the claim itself is unchanged.

proposed.statement:
For \(\ell=3\), \(r_\beta(3)=4\).  There is a Zariski-dense relatively Euclidean-open subset \(\mathcal S\subseteq\mathcal O_{3,3}\) such that every \(\zeta\in\mathcal S\) has at least one preimage \(\theta\in\Theta_{3,3}\) satisfying
\[
 \operatorname{rank}D(\Phi_{3,3},\beta)(\theta)=17
 >16=\operatorname{rank}D\Phi_{3,3}(\theta),
\]
and \(F_{3,3}(\zeta)\) contains a real legal curve along which \(\beta\) varies.  At order four, \(\mathfrak A^{\mathrm{id}}_{3,4}\ne\varnothing\), and the union of its domains \(\mathcal U_\chi\cap\mathcal O_{3,4}\) contains a nonempty relatively Zariski-open subset; every covering chart returns the common legal-fiber effect, while outside all chart domains every recovery map returns \(\bot\).  Consequently the three-latent workflow may replace \(C_{\le k(3)}=C_{\le7}\) by \(C_{\le4}\) on the regular legal image, whereas \(C_{\le3}\) does not generically identify a point effect on \(\mathcal S\).
proposed.justification: The exact three-latent case converts a fiber calculation into a seven-to-four reduction in required empirical cumulant order and a sharp order-three nonidentification decision.
proposed.gap: Tramontano et al., Theorems 3.4--3.5, specialize to the sufficient order \(k(3)=7\) and do not show either order-four sufficiency from the complete tensor or generic failure at order three.
proposed.consumer: For \(\ell=3\), CEId-from-Moments can stop after estimating \(C_{\le4}\) instead of \(C_{\le7}\); if only \(C_{\le3}\) is available on the open lower-fiber locus, it must return nonidentification rather than a selected point estimate.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The orchestrator requires the class bridge in the three-latent comparison to the published sufficient order; the claim itself is unchanged.

proposed.statement: Determine the finite value of \(r_\beta(\ell)\) exactly for every \(\ell\ge4\).  Using \(\mathfrak H_{\ell}\), classify each unresolved intermediate order \(L_\ell\le R<U_\ell\).  At every order where \(\beta\) is generically constant on legal fibers, give a terminating algebraic recovery atlas whose domains cover a nonempty relatively Zariski-open subset of \(\mathcal O_{\ell,R}\), whose covering charts return the common effect, and whose uncovered legal inputs return \(\bot\).  At every smaller unresolved order, construct a Zariski-dense relatively Euclidean-open subset of the legal image whose fibers contain independent finite-support unequal-\(\beta\) twins.  The first remaining elbow is \((\ell,R)=(4,3)\): decide its complete saturated target projection and certify every surviving real branch against the finite-atomic moment constraints.  The established exact values are \(r_\beta(1)=r_\beta(2)=3\) and \(r_\beta(3)=4\), so none of these cases remains part of the question.
proposed.justification: This residual theorem-level kernel asks for the exact finite frontier after the one-, two-, and three-latent cases have been closed.
proposed.gap: The closest paper supplies only \(k(\ell)\)-order sufficiency, and no exact all-\(\ell\ge4\) complete-cumulant fiber frontier is known.
proposed.consumer: The result would fix every remaining minimum moment order and the associated failure certificate used by the companion estimator.

obligation.what_is_open: Determine \(r_\beta(\ell)\) for every remaining \(\ell\ge4\), beginning with the complete legal target projection at \((\ell,R)=(4,3)\).
obligation.obstruction: The two-latent finite branch is eliminated exactly, but the upper and lower constructions do not classify all remaining intermediate orders.
obligation.attempted: The prescribed \((2,3)\) elbow was reduced to a linear observable target equation; no inference about the different \((4,3)\) geometry was made.
obligation.partial_result:
The complete \((\ell,R)=(2,3)\) target projection is now closed.  On the observable chart \(\Delta_{2,3}=\det(M_3)a_1\ne0\), the polynomial \(\mathcal P_\zeta(q)\) factors as
\[
 \mathcal P_\zeta(q)=\det(M_3)(\beta-q)
 \left\{\kappa^S_{t,2}-\kappa^S_{t,3}\lambda_2^{\mathsf T}
 \Lambda_3^{-1}V^{-1}(0,1,0)^{\mathsf T}\right\}.
\]
Thus its target rational-univariate representation is linear, every legal representation has \(\beta=-a_0/a_1\), and the unequal-effect incidence localization is empty.  The explicit legal point in the proof has \(\mathcal P_\zeta(q)=50(2-q)\) and \(\Delta_{2,3}=-300\).  Consequently
\[
 r_\beta(1)=3,\qquad r_\beta(2)=3,\qquad r_\beta(3)=4,
\]
while the established global bounds remain
\[
 L_\ell\le r_\beta(\ell)\le U_\ell,
 \qquad \frac{r_\beta(\ell)}{\sqrt{2\ell}}\longrightarrow1.
\]
The unresolved finite cases begin at \((\ell,R)=(4,3)\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: This is the metadata-complete post-image for the narrowed residual question and wires in the newly proved two-latent theorem and class bridge.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: For an established contraction chart, \(g_{\chi}(C_{\le R})=\beta=C_{d_{\chi}+2}[f_{\chi},T,Y]/C_{d_{\chi}+2}[f_{\chi},T,T]\) on \(\mathcal U_{\chi}\), and it returns \(\bot\) otherwise. For \(\ell=2\) and \(R\ge3\), the additional order-three map in the two-latent depth theorem returns \(-a_0(C_{\le3})/a_1(C_{\le3})\) when \(\det(M_3)a_1(C_{\le3})\ne0\), and returns \(\bot\) otherwise; here \(a_0,a_1\) are the displayed observable coefficients of \(\mathcal P_\zeta\).
proposed_core_edits.reason: The headline functional must include the newly proved order-three two-latent recovery map and its instability certificate in addition to the contraction atlas.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Determine \(r_\beta(\ell)\) for every remaining \(\ell\ge4\), beginning with the complete legal target projection at \((\ell,R)=(4,3)\).
open_obligations.obstruction: The two-latent finite branch is now eliminated exactly, but neither the contraction upper bound nor the weight-saturation lower construction classifies the intermediate orders \(L_\ell\le R<U_\ell\) for all \(\ell\ge4\). Those fibers can mix positive-dimensional loading variation with discrete decomposition branches, and their target projection and real moment feasibility have not yet been certified.
open_obligations.attempted: The prescribed first elbow \((2,3)\) was reduced to an observable covariance--third-cumulant identity. Its linear factorization proved that the unequal-effect saturation is empty on a nonempty legal chart, so the proposed open-twin architecture was correctly abandoned there. No claim about the still different \((4,3)\) incidence geometry is inferred from that calculation.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The complete \((\ell,R)=(2,3)\) target projection is now closed.  On the observable chart \(\Delta_{2,3}=\det(M_3)a_1\ne0\), the polynomial \(\mathcal P_\zeta(q)\) factors as
\[
 \mathcal P_\zeta(q)=\det(M_3)(\beta-q)
 \left\{\kappa^S_{t,2}-\kappa^S_{t,3}\lambda_2^{\mathsf T}
 \Lambda_3^{-1}V^{-1}(0,1,0)^{\mathsf T}\right\}.
\]
Thus its target rational-univariate representation is linear, every legal representation has \(\beta=-a_0/a_1\), and the unequal-effect incidence localization is empty.  The explicit legal point in the proof has \(\mathcal P_\zeta(q)=50(2-q)\) and \(\Delta_{2,3}=-300\).  Consequently
\[
 r_\beta(1)=3,\qquad r_\beta(2)=3,\qquad r_\beta(3)=4,
\]
while the established global bounds remain
\[
 L_\ell\le r_\beta(\ell)\le U_\ell,
 \qquad \frac{r_\beta(\ell)}{\sqrt{2\ell}}\longrightarrow1.
\]
The unresolved finite cases begin at \((\ell,R)=(4,3)\).

prose_updates.tldr: Higher-order cumulants identify the treatment effect in the fixed single-proxy latent-confounded LiNGAM, but the published order \(k(\ell)\) is only sufficient. The proved frontier now has exact depths \(r_\beta(1)=r_\beta(2)=3\) and \(r_\beta(3)=4\), global bounds with matching square-root asymptotics, and terminating algebraic recovery maps with explicit instability certificates. The mandatory complete \((\ell,R)=(2,3)\) test has a linear target eliminant: on \(\det(M_3)a_1\ne0\), every legal representation has \(\beta=-a_0/a_1\), and the unequal-effect incidence saturation is empty. Exact finite depths for \(\ell\ge4\) remain open, beginning at \((4,3)\). The class bridge distinguishes the paper's centered, realizable finite-atomic truncation from Tramontano et al.'s larger unrestricted diagonal-cumulant chart while showing that finite-support converse twins transfer to their actual-law class and that the upper contraction algebra transfers to their generic chart.

project_justification.gap: Tramontano et al. prove proxy-effect identification through the bivariate recovery order \(k(\ell)\), with \(k(2)=6\), but do not determine the minimum depth of the complete ternary cumulant law. Their algebraic generic chart treats diagonal cumulants as unrestricted coordinates, whereas the present legal domain also enforces positive variances and simultaneous centered moment realizability. Before this result, the generically finite \((2,3)\) map left open a disconnected legal unequal-effect branch.
project_justification.niche: The graph's distinguished treatment and outcome disturbance directions allow a mixed covariance identity to be interpolated through the invertible proxy-anchored third-cumulant matrix. For two latents this produces a linear observable target eliminant even though no degree-one proxy annihilator exists.
project_justification.fill: The paper proves \(r_\beta(2)=3\) by the explicit map \(-a_0/a_1\), certifies the exceptional locus by \(\det(M_3)a_1=0\), and proves that the localized unequal-effect incidence ideal is empty. Together with the established one- and three-latent cases, the exact values are now three, three, and four for \(\ell=1,2,3\). The global bounds and square-root asymptotics remain, while exact intermediate-order classification for \(\ell\ge4\) is retained as the honest frontier. For the companion implementation, the two-latent minimum input falls from the published sufficient order six to order three and gains a determinant-slope instability report.

prose_updates.related_work: Tramontano et al. (2025, Theorem 3.1) use a degree-\(\ell+1\) bivariate loading-root polynomial through \(k(\ell)\); Theorems 3.4--3.5 align the resulting proxy loading lists and prove effect sufficiency at that order. Their unrestricted diagonal-cumulant parameterization is the algebraic ambient chart, while the present \(\Theta_{\ell,R}\) is a centered, generic-nonzero, actual-law truncation with positive variance and simultaneous cross-order realizability. The class bridge shows exactly what transfers in each direction. For \(\ell=2\), the published workflow uses \(k(2)=6\), whereas the new complete-tensor identity gives the sharp order three and rules out a separate nonsingular legal target branch. For \(\ell=3\), the established sharp order is four rather than \(k(3)=7\). Theorem 3.6 of Tramontano et al. claims order-three nonidentification for one latent; the established one-latent theorem instead gives order-three full-fiber recovery and audits the extra algebraic root against the legal moment domain. Schkoda, Robeva, and Drton (2024) supply the bivariate root machinery, while Garcia-Puente, Spielvogel, and Sullivant (2010) supply the target-elimination viewpoint; neither gives the mixed covariance--third-cumulant linear target certificate proved here. Full-distribution overcomplete independent-component results and the banked bivariate causal-direction frontier concern different targets and do not settle this fixed-graph minimum complete-cumulant depth.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The complete \((2,3)\) beta projection is settled on the explicit nonempty legal chart \(\det(M_3)a_1\ne0\): its target rational-univariate representation is linear over both the real and complex fibers, so there is no second positive-variance branch there. The result does not claim that the proxy-annihilator atlas itself works at order three for two latents; the new mixed covariance--third-cumulant map is a separate terminating chart and is included explicitly in the estimand functional. The established contraction theorem still supplies the all-\(\ell\) upper depth \(U_\ell\), and finite-support lower twins transfer to the published actual-law class, but the unrestricted diagonal algebraic chart is larger than the realizable moment domain. Exact depths for \(\ell\ge4\) and legal-real fibers at unresolved intermediate orders remain open, beginning with \((4,3)\). The bivariate causal-direction minimum-order frontier is distinct: it orients an arrow between two observed variables, whereas this paper fixes the single-proxy graph and identifies the interventional coefficient \(\beta\) from the complete trivariate cumulant map.
